name: Baptist Churches: Beginnings and Splits
summary: How the Baptist churches began among English Separatists in exile in 1609 and divided over theology, missions, slavery, race, and the authority of Scripture.

start.label: John Smyth baptizes himself and his English Separatist congregation in Amsterdam

end.label: Moderates leave the Southern Baptist Convention to form the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship

key_dates.label: Thomas Helwys founds the first Baptist church in England and appeals for religious liberty
Roger Williams founds the first Baptist church in America at Providence
First London Confession of the Calvinistic (Particular) Baptists
Triennial Convention organizes American Baptist foreign missions
Black Rock Address: anti-mission (Primitive) Baptists separate
Southern Baptist Convention formed over slavery
National Baptist Convention, U.S.A. unites Black Baptists
Fundamentalists leave the Northern Baptists to form the GARBC
'Conservative Resurgence' begins in the Southern Baptist Convention

background.text: Baptists grew out of English Puritan Separatism. They are distinct in origin from the Continental Anabaptists of 1525, though Smyth's group had contact with Dutch Mennonites.

happened.text: John Smyth's congregation in Amsterdam adopted believers' baptism in 1609; Thomas Helwys led part of it back to London in 1612, forming the 'General Baptists', who held that Christ died for all.
Calvinistic 'Particular Baptists' arose in London in the 1630s, adopted immersion, and issued the London Confessions of 1644 and 1689.
In America Baptists were a persecuted minority until the Revolution, then grew rapidly in the Great Awakenings, especially in the South and among enslaved and free Black Americans.
Disputes over mission societies, slavery, race, and liberal theology repeatedly divided Baptists, who have no central authority over local congregations.

participants.name: John Smyth
participants.role: Founder of the first English Baptist congregation (Amsterdam)

participants.name: Thomas Helwys
participants.role: Founder of the first Baptist church in England

participants.name: Roger Williams
participants.role: Founder of Rhode Island and the first American Baptist church

participants.name: William Carey
participants.role: Founder of the Baptist Missionary Society (1792) and missionary to India

participants.name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
participants.role: Leading 19th-century Particular Baptist preacher; left the Baptist Union in the Down-Grade Controversy (1887)

outcomes.text: Baptists became one of the largest Protestant families, with the Southern Baptist Convention the largest Protestant denomination in the United States.
Their early insistence on religious liberty and separation of church and state influenced the First Amendment and later democratic thought.

condemnations_note: Baptist congregations are independent, so divisions came by withdrawal and exclusion from associations rather than formal excommunication by a central body.

persecution_note: Early Baptists were persecuted by both church and state in England and colonial America.

persecution.title: Imprisonment of Thomas Helwys
persecution.summary: Helwys published A Short Declaration of the Mystery of Iniquity, the first English plea for full religious liberty, and sent a signed copy to King James I telling him he had no power over people's souls. He was imprisoned in Newgate and died there about 1616.

persecution.title: Imprisonment of John Bunyan and Restoration penalties
persecution.summary: After the Restoration, laws against nonconformist worship were used against Baptists; the Baptist preacher John Bunyan spent about 12 years in Bedford jail for unlicensed preaching, where he wrote Grace Abounding.

responsible.name: Charles II's government and local magistrates

persecution.outcome: Released in 1672 under the Declaration of Indulgence.

persecution.title: Whipping of Obadiah Holmes in Boston
persecution.summary: Massachusetts authorities fined the Baptists John Clarke, Obadiah Holmes, and John Crandall for holding a service; Holmes refused to let his fine be paid and was publicly whipped with 30 lashes.
persecution.outcome: Whipped; John Clarke's account helped win toleration for Baptists in Rhode Island's charter (1663).

persecution.title: Jailing of Baptist preachers in Virginia
persecution.summary: Some 30 or more Baptist preachers were jailed in Anglican Virginia for preaching without licenses, some preaching through the bars to crowds outside.

responsible.name: Virginia county courts and Anglican establishment

persecution.outcome: Fed the campaign of James Madison and Thomas Jefferson for religious freedom (Virginia statute, 1786).
